title: Confirmed (severity corrected to medium): unauthenticated, indefinite management-plane lockout — username-keyed 5-attempt lock whose counter is never reset when the lock expires, and whose only in-band recovery API is gated behind the session of the account being denied
evidence: Verified verbatim at the cited lines. backend/internal/admin/auth.go:114 `func (s *Server) onMFAFail(u *model.AdminUser) {` with 115-121: `u.FailedLogins++` / `updates := map[string]any{"failed_logins": u.FailedLogins}` / `if u.FailedLogins >= 5 {` / `loc := time.Now().Add(15 * time.Minute)` / `updates["locked_until"] = loc` / `s.db.Model(&model.AdminUser{}).Where("id = ?", u.ID).Updates(updates)`. First-factor use: auth.go:76-79 `if err := bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(u.PasswordHash), []byte(req.Password)); err != nil { s.onMFAFail(&u);`. Lock gate evaluated before any credential check: auth.go:38-41 `if u.IsLocked() { s.fail(c, http.StatusForbidden, 40301, "账户已被锁定，请稍后再试或联系管理员解锁")` — so attempts during an active lock do not extend it, it always lapses on schedule. Expiry test: model.go:28-30 `func (u *AdminUser) IsLocked() bool { return u.LockedUntil != nil && time.Now().Before(*u.LockedUntil) }` (no counter reset, no state change). Counter cleared in exactly two places — auth.go:81-83 `u.FailedLogins = 0` + `Update("failed_logins", 0)` (successful login only) and users.go:61-62 `Updates(map[string]any{"failed_logins": 0, "locked_until": nil})`. Repo-wide grep for `FailedLogins|failed_logins|LockedUntil|locked_until|IsLocked` returns only auth.go:38/81/83/115/116/117/119, model.go:21/22/28/29, users.go:27/62 — i.e. no sweeper job anywhere (quota.go:243-264 resets only quotas and limiter hits) and no code path that disarms the counter when a lock expires. Unthrottled route: routes.go:42 `api.POST("/auth/login", s.login)` (every sibling route from routes.go:43 on carries `s.AuthMiddleware()`), and main.go:89-118 registers only `engine.Use(gin.Recovery())` plus a security-header closure and an access-log closure. The only limiter in the tree is data-plane scoped: quota/quota.go:33-36 `type Limiter interface { Allow(snap *runtime.Snapshot, apiKeyID uint, alias string) ... }`, windows keyed `fmt.Sprintf("%d:%d:%s", r.ID, apiKeyID, alias)` (quota.go:67), sole wiring main.go:121 `gw := gateway.New(gormDB, mgr, bl, rl, qm, al, mx)`. No configurable threshold: settings.go:79-84 `type Security struct { MFAEnabled bool; MFARequiredAll bool; RecoveryCodeCount int; GraceDays int }`. No lock alert: onMFAFail performs no `recordOp`, and the only webhook in the codebase is quota.go:216-223. Target is known by default: config.go:65 `AdminUser:          getenv("ADMIN_USER", "admin")`, created by main.go:164-183, bound on all interfaces at main.go:126 `srv := &http.Server{Addr: fmt.Sprintf(":%d", cfg.ListenPort), Handler: engine}`.
impact: Availability, management plane, indefinite. An unauthenticated request with the username `admin` and any wrong password increments a per-account counter that is keyed to the username, never to the source address, and is not bounded by any throttle: 5 requests from anywhere on the network lock the console. Because `failed_logins` survives lock expiry at 5, the single next wrong password re-arms a fresh 15-minute lock; with unthrottled hammering the re-arm latency after each expiry is milliseconds, so the account is locked effectively 100% of wall-clock time and the legitimate admin's correct password always hits auth.go:38 before it can reach the reset at auth.go:81-83. There is no in-band recovery: routes.go:135 `api.POST("/users/:id/unlock", s.AuthMiddleware(), s.unlockUser)` demands a session of the very account being denied, and no route can create a second admin (routes.go:133-135 offers only GET /users, unbind-mfa, unlock; there is no POST /users), so `bootstrapAdmin` (main.go:164-183) leaves a single-account system by design. Recovery therefore requires direct SQLite access (`UPDATE admin_users SET failed_logins=0, locked_until=NULL`) or POST /backups/restore, and restarting the process does not help because the state is persistent. Nothing logs or alerts on the transition (onMFAFail writes no OperationLog and no failed login is audited), so the loss can persist unnoticed. Incident-response consequence: while locked out the operator cannot rotate a leaked provider key, disable an abused `sk-` gateway key, inspect call/operation audit, or rollback config — while an attacker's already-issued 24h JWT remains fully valid (authn-2) and gateway traffic continues unaffected (backend/internal/gateway has zero references to AdminUser/failed_logins). Scope limits the rating: no credential, session, or secret is disclosed or gained; the data plane keeps serving; the state is reversible with one SQL UPDATE once understood. Under this engagement's taxonomy (high = authed-but-severe or account takeover) that is medium — a defense-in-depth gap with real, trivially-triggered, persistent impact — not high. Two parts of the original narrative are corrected rather than refuted: (a) 'a cron job sending one bogus password every ~15 minutes denies the admin indefinitely' does not hold, since one successful login anywhere in the open window resets the budget to 5; the permanent form of the DoS needs continuous attempts, which the absent limiter enables; (b) the event is not fully invisible — client.ts:79-80 `if (bizMessage) { message.error(bizMessage) }` does surface the raw '账户已被锁定…' message in the UI; what is missing is any *proactive* notification.
mitigations_checked: The lockout is a specified control (prd.md:362 REQ-022 ② '连续 5 次失败后锁定账户', docs/api-contract.md:47), so username-keyed locking per se is intended design; the defect is the never-disarmed counter plus the absence of any address-scoped throttle. Genuinely mitigating: it does not extend while locked (auth.go:38 early-return), so the lock is self-healing absent further attempts; the same handler also covers second-factor failures (auth.go:67, auth.go:104), so TOTP/recovery-code guessing is throttled; recovery codes are hashed (auth.go:245) so a lock cannot be bypassed there. Checked and NOT mitigating: no login middleware (middleware.go is 33 lines of JWT parsing only — its header comment '速率辅助' is stale); no nginx/LB/fail2ban config ships in the repo (grep `limit_req|rate.?limit|fail2ban|iptables|max_conn`); `General.MaxConnections` is enforced only in gateway.go:195, never on /api/admin/v1; `SetMaxOpenConns(1)` (db.go:52) serializes SQLite writes but has no effect on the lock lifecycle; the authn-4 read-modify-write race weakens triggering slightly (concurrent bursts advance the counter by ~1) and is irrelevant given unbounded attempts; `/users/:id/unlock` is unreachable for the victim.
recommendation: (1) Put a per-IP and per-(username,IP) token bucket in front of routes.go:42 (reuse the existing in-memory window or the shared mfaStore/Redis `INCR`+`EXPIRE`, which is already multi-instance plumbing); TRUSTED_PROXIES stays empty by default, so `c.ClientIP()` is already a trustworthy key for this route. (2) End the counter's life with the lock: at auth.go:38, when `u.LockedUntil != nil && !time.Now().Before(*u.LockedUntil)`, lazily persist `failed_logins = 0, locked_until = nil` before continuing — a lazy reset needs no background sweeper. (3) Make 5/15m configurable in settings.Security alongside MFA knobs and add an admin IP allowlist for /auth/login as defense-in-depth. (4) Record and alert the lock transition: `s.recordOp(c, "lock", "security", ...)` inside onMFAFail plus a webhook reusing the quota.go:222 channel; audit failed logins at all (currently zero rows). (5) Provide an out-of-band recovery that does not require the denied session — e.g. a `--unlock-admin <username>` CLI subcommand or a documented single-command SQL recipe in quickstart, and fix the missing user-creation route so a second administrator is possible at all. (6) Uniformize the pre-auth response envelope (also fixes the authn-5 oracle) so a lock cannot be used as an existence probe.

title: The same missing login throttle makes /auth/login an unauthenticated bcrypt CPU/concurrency amplifier: every random wrong password forces a full cost-10 hash comparison with no per-IP, per-route, or global connection bound
evidence: auth.go:76 `if err := bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(u.PasswordHash), []byte(req.Password)); err != nil {` runs for every request that carries a known username, before any failure bookkeeping, and routes.go:42 `api.POST("/auth/login", s.login)` has no middleware in front of it. The stored hash sets the work factor at bcrypt's default: main.go:175 `hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(pass), bcrypt.DefaultCost)` (cost 10) and auth.go:180 `bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(req.NewPassword), bcrypt.DefaultCost)`. No global bound exists: main.go:126 `srv := &http.Server{Addr: fmt.Sprintf(":%d", cfg.ListenPort), Handler: engine}` sets only Addr/Handler (dos-4 covers the missing timeouts), and grep for `MaxConnections` yields just gateway.go:195, settings.go:19, settings.go:32 — the concurrency budget is a gateway-handler check, not a server limit. Because the username is known by default (config.go:65 `getenv("ADMIN_USER", "admin")`), no reconnaissance is needed to reach the expensive branch, unlike the 404-on-unknown-user path at auth.go:34-37 which short-circuits before bcrypt.
impact: Cheap unauthenticated CPU burn on the same single process that terminates all gateway traffic and holds the SQLite writer, so an attacker does not need to hit /v1/* at all to degrade routing latency: a handful of parallel loops against one route pins N cores in bcrypt and serializes the admin DB writes behind `SetMaxOpenConns(1)` (db.go:52). It also amplifies verify-authn-3-1 by letting the attacker re-arm the 15-minute lock within milliseconds of each expiry. Bounded, and therefore low: the cost is per-connection (one request = one comparison), it is the same work factor every bcrypt deployment accepts, and the effect is latency/CPU pressure rather than data loss — which is why it is filed as an additional consequence of the verified 'no throttle on /auth/login' fact rather than as a separate high item.
mitigations_checked: bcrypt (not a fast hash) is used correctly; unknown usernames short-circuit before any comparison (auth.go:34-37), so the loop must spend nothing on dead names; `ReadTimeout: 90 * time.Second` (config.go:72) is set on the config object but per dos-4 is never applied to the http.Server, so it does not cap this; no CAPTCHA, no account-agnostic early reject, no body-size or per-connection request cap on the admin group.
recommendation: The per-IP limiter recommended in verify-authn-3-1 closes this too. Additionally: cap concurrent in-flight login handlers with a small semaphore (e.g. 2-4) around s.login so bcrypt work cannot fan out across all cores; and if bcrypt cost must stay at 10 for interactive logins, keep it there but never expose the comparison to unthrottled network input.

title: Login UI misses the lock status code: a 403/40301 lockout is rendered as 'network error' next to the leaked 'account locked' toast, so a victim of the lockout DoS misdiagnoses an attack as connectivity and retries — re-arming the lock
evidence: Login.tsx:64-71 `const status = (e as { response?: { status?: number } }).response?.status; const code = (e as { code?: number }).code; if (status === 401 || code === 40101 || code === 40102 || code === 40103) { message.error(t('login.invalidCredentials')); } else { // 网络错误 / 超时等，非鉴权失败，不伪装成账密错误 message.error(t('common.networkError')); }`. The backend lock answer is HTTP 403 with code 40301 (auth.go:39 `s.fail(c, http.StatusForbidden, 40301, "账户已被锁定，请稍后再试或联系管理员解锁")`), which matches neither list, so control falls to the else branch. It also arrives as a non-2xx response, so it is handled by the error interceptor, not by the envelope branch: client.ts:73-83 `const status = error.response?.status; const bizMessage = error.response?.data?.message; if (status === 401) { redirectToLogin(); return Promise.reject(error); } if (bizMessage) { message.error(bizMessage); }` — meaning the raw server message *is* displayed. Two toasts therefore contradict each other ('account locked' + 'network error'). The comment at Login.tsx:62-63 states the intent is '账密错误 / MFA 码错误 / 账户锁定等统一提示，不暴露具体原因（防枚举）', which the interceptor defeats. The lock contract code is documented at docs/api-contract.md:373 `| 40301 | 403 | 无权限/账户锁定 |`.
impact: Availability-incident diagnosability, not direct compromise. The only signal a locked-out sole admin receives is contradictory, and 'network error' points them at the wrong layer (proxy, TLS, firewall) while the real state is a DB column they cannot reach through the UI (see verify-authn-3-1: /users/:id/unlock is behind the auth they just lost, and no log row records the lock). A retry loop is the natural human response to 'network error', and each retry after expiry immediately re-arms the 15-minute lock, so the UX bug actively extends the attacker's window. It also means the console's Security page (frontend/src/pages/settings/Security.tsx:148-179, which does render `locked` and an Unlock button) is unreachable exactly when it would explain the situation.
mitigations_checked: The server message is still shown by the interceptor, so the information is not wholly suppressed (this corrects the 'no visibility' phrasing in the original authn-3 impact); the 401 path is handled deliberately (client.ts:75-78) and the login page intentionally avoids enumerating credential failures (Login.tsx:62-67); no XSS/secret exposure exists in rendering `bizMessage` (antd message escapes its text child). Not a duplicate of authn-5, which is about the *server* oracle — this item is the client's mishandling of the same response.
recommendation: Handle 403/40301 explicitly in Login.tsx with a distinct, non-alarming message ('this account is temporarily locked; contact the operator or wait until <locked_until>') and stop the double toast by having client.ts:79-81 mark the error as already-reported (e.g. set `err.notified = true` and skip in the caller). Better, return the remaining lock duration from the API so the operator can tell an attack (repeated 403s with a fresh lock each cycle) from a typo, and pair it with the lock-event audit row recommended in verify-authn-3-1.
